title: fix(pm): post-stamped refuses a declared reading at the two positions H56 reads
body:
Fixes #18995

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` claimed in its own header that its positional refusal "refuses exactly what the read-side patrol would file". The card falsified that twice, on live artefacts written by *following* the header's own prescription. This makes the claim true.

## The defect, reproduced on the base

The positional walk ran the patrol's `h56StampedReadings` over `maskQuotedStamps`'d text, where a declared reading is blanked. So a declared-reading token (the `WAS` spelling) on the artefact's OPENING line, or on a subscript reading-time line, passed the write side — and the POSITIONAL refusal text offered that spelling there by name. `substituteTokens` then renders a declaration as its payload and nothing else, so the declaration is spent at render time and the board carries bare digits at a position H56 reads as the writing act's own clock.

Measured on `744a0a3` before the change, with the card's own two numbers:

| body | write side | what renders at the position | H56 drift vs the stored instant |
|---|---|---|---|
| opening line declaring a card's close time | ACCEPTED, 0 refusals | `2026-09-18T09:04Z` | 19 min — filed |
| subscript reading-time line declaring a CI-log reading | ACCEPTED, 0 refusals | `2026-09-19T07:58Z` | 22 min — filed |

Both PM mechanism assumptions hold as stated. H1: `substituteTokens` emits the payload alone, so the declaration is erased at post time and no downstream reader can recover it. H2: the positional walk over masked text finds 0 readings on that opening line while the rendered body carries 1, on both positions.

## The change

The positional judgement now runs over the body `substituteTokens` will actually send, through the same imported reader. A stamp standing at either position that is not this act's own clock is refused whichever spelling put it there — a new refusal kind `positional-declared`, whose remedy is the act-clock token at the position with the quoted reading moved into the body. The bare-stamp POSITIONAL remedy stops offering the declared route AT the position and prescribes it in the body instead, so no refusal text prescribes a refused remedy.

Two shapes are deliberately left alone, both because the patrol leaves them alone:

- a position carrying MORE THAN ONE stamp once rendered (the act-clock token beside a declared reading on one line) — H56 holds that line out rather than guess, and so does this;
- a declaration whose value IS this act's clock minute — it renders the bytes the act-clock token would have written, so refusing it would make the parity claim false the other way round.

The bare scan is untouched and stays value-free: a typed stamp equal to this act's own minute is still typed, and is still refused. A declaration the value rules already refused is not ALSO filed here — one typo, one refusal, the rule this file already states for the calendar and direction checks.

## Parity pin

A new declared self-test battery, "the two positions: a declaration renders as bare digits, and the patrol reads digits", registers 17 cases and is pinned at 17 in `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES` (floor rules unchanged; the roster floor stays at 15). Every row asserts one body against BOTH halves: what `stampRefusals` does with it, and what `h56EstimatedStamp` — imported, not restated — would file on the bytes that body renders to. Declared reading on the opening line and on a subscript line: refused, and would be filed. Act-clock token at either position, the same declaration one line down, a rendered position carrying two stamps, and a declaration whose value is this act's clock: accepted, and the patrol is silent.

Fixture triage, per disposition rather than a batch respelling: the one case that pinned the acceptance itself ("a DECLARED quoted stamp is accepted even in the opening position") is replaced by the pair that reads in both directions; five one-line fixtures whose subject is the calendar or direction rule, and which put a declaration in the opening position only because they were one-liners, are moved off that line.

## Reverse verification — one-time, nothing left in the tree

Both legs ran from the committed state through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, so the mutation is proven on disk (anchor count and blob hash) rather than by an editor's exit code.

Leg A — revert the walk's input to the masked text, which is exactly the pre-fix behaviour:

```
ablation-replace: anchor "h56StampedReadings(substituteTokens(raw, now, spans).body)" x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: blob bd4827ab78bf -> dafbf9e6e0cf
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed
x post-stamped self-test: 7 of 562 case(s) failed, 0 floor problem(s).
```

The seven are the parity rows by name, including "THE FILED REPRO", "PARITY", and "the SECOND position the card measured". Direction observed: turned red, the ordinary direction.

Leg B — remove the act-clock exemption (`hit.stamp === now`). The suite goes red by CRASH, at an existing unrelated case whose body stops rendering, which is itself the evidence the exemption is load-bearing; it is reported as a crash, not as a row-level reading.

Both legs restored by the tool and re-checked by hand: worktree blob equals the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates, at `d12550d`

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` (no paths; the script takes its own change set from the merge base) and reconciled with `--ran`:

```
Run reconciliation - 30 derived, 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
EXIT CODES - all 30 accounted famil(ies) carry one.
```

Every one exited 0, `pnpm check:pm-post-stamped` (the file's own `--self-test`, 562 cases across 19 batteries) and `pnpm check:nul-bytes` among them. Three families outside the derivation were run because this diff reaches them through imports: `close-cards.mjs --self-test` (102 cases, it imports `renderBody`), `write-pace.mjs --self-test` (69 cases) and `check-half-states.mjs --self-test` (5160 cases, the other half of this contract) — all exit 0.

The 55 artifact-roster families, the 11 wide-population families, the 14 pending-changeset families and the one path-scheduled CI job the derivation names are outside that total and are CI's.

## Lint, narrowed and declared

`pnpm lint` is `eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole tree and belongs to CI. What ran here is the same binary and the same flag over the one changed file, with the three readings that make a narrowing a measurement rather than a skip:

1. the population is whatever `eslint .` reaches under `eslint.config.mjs` — read from that config, not guessed;
2. `--format json` reports 1 file linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings, and `git diff --name-only` against the merge base names exactly that 1 file;
3. that config enables no type-aware linting for ANY file. Its own header states it: "this repo runs one `eslint.config.mjs`, which never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file, test or not." So nothing in this diff can move the verdict on a file it did not touch, and the narrowing excludes nothing.

`turbo ls --affected` is not cited: the repo-root package is not in the turbo graph at all, so this path is not on it.

## Acceptance notes

- **The card's second same-family defect is no longer reachable on this base.** The card reported 11 refusals while writing its own body, 8 of them `quoted-not-a-stamp` raised by quoting the token verbatim, plus UNKNOWN-opener refusals when the token was split across backticks. Measured here with the spellings the card lists: the placeholder form inside a code span beside an act-clock token is ACCEPTED, and so is the split-into-backticks workaround (0 openers flagged). The residue — a declared token carrying REAL DIGITS, quoted beside the act-clock token, still taking the MIXED refusal — is a deliberate decision recorded in the header of that file ("deliberately NOT made quote-aware"), and its fenced-block half belongs to #19319, which remains open, is p3 and `pm:queue`, and is out of scope here. Nothing in this PR touches it.
- **Rejected alternative, recorded and not built:** render a marker H56 recognises. It is a third spelling both halves must learn, visible on the board, bought to keep a reading in the one position where no reader can tell it from the act's own clock. The position is the defect; a marker makes it survivable instead of removing it. No legitimate seat artefact was found whose opening line MUST carry a quoted reading — the card's own remediation was to move the reading into the body, which is what the new refusal prescribes.
- **`skip-changeset`:** `scripts/pm/**` is on the fast-track list and publishes nothing from any released package; no package `files[]` ships this path.
- **Line budget:** net +124 (135 insertions, 11 deletions) against the dispatch's +120. Two trimming passes removed the table of what the rule buys and three lines of restated comment. The remaining 4 lines are the header's rejected-route paragraph, which the file's own convention keeps beside every other rejected route; it fits within budget only if that paragraph lives in this PR body alone, and that trade is the reviewer's to make, not this run's to take silently.
- **H56 semantics are untouched.** `check-half-states.mjs` is imported only; `h56EstimatedStamp` is the one symbol this change adds to the import list, for the parity pin.

## How a caller sees it

A body whose opening line declares a reading of something else is refused before any request, with the position named, the declaration quoted, the digits it would have rendered to shown, and the remedy spelled: the act-clock token there, the reading in the body.
